text:
maria: Hey, seeing a bunch of connect failures from our inference pods to the PrivateLink interface endpoint for our model-registry service. curl just hangs and TLS times out. Started ~09:12 UTC. Anyone else?
jon: Which endpoint? vpce id or dns name?
maria: vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-model-registry.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com
aditya: Can you paste `dig +short` and `curl -v` output?
maria: `dig +short vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-model-registry.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com` -> `10.0.45.12`
maria: `curl -v https://vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-model-registry.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health` -> `* Connected to 10.0.45.12 port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout`
jon: TLS handshake timeout to endpoint IP usually means connection hits ENI but SG blocks the return, or packet loss. Can you `kubectl exec` into a pod and `traceroute` to that IP?
maria: running `kubectl exec -it infer-0 -- traceroute -n 10.0.45.12` -> traceroute shows one hop directly to node then stops.
aditya: Ok. Check the endpoint ENIs' security group. `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values*vpce* Name=tag:Name,Values=*model-registry* --query 'NetworkInterfaces[].[NetworkInterfaceId,PrivateIpAddress,Groups]'`
maria: got ENI ids and SG=sg-0f4a1c2b. Private IPs are in the same AZ as the pods' nodes.
aditya: What's the SG ingress on sg-0f4a1c2b?
maria: ingress only allows TCP 443 from 10.0.0.0/16 (our VPC primary CIDR).
jon: Are pod IPs in a different CIDR? If pod IPs are preserved as source and not SNATed, endpoint will see pod CIDR and SG will drop.
maria: Our pods are 192.168.0.0/16 (Calico overlay), and nodes are 10.0.x.x. I think we're preserving source IPs (we turned off SNAT for hostPort reasons).
aditya: Bingo. Endpoint SG only allows 10.0.0.0/16 so packets from 192.168.0.0/16 are dropped. Two options: 1) add pod CIDR to endpoint SG (quick), 2) re-enable SNAT so source is node IP (more global). Which is acceptable?
maria: Quick fix to unblock: add 192.168.0.0/16 ingress on sg-0f4a1c2b? Any objections?
jon: That's fine temporarily but we should avoid adding wide CIDR to infra-owned SGs. Add the exact pod CIDR used by the cluster and annotate for cleanup.
aditya: I'll add a rule `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0f4a1c2b --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 192.168.0.0/16` now, will report back.
infra-bot: deploy: security-group-update-job started by aditya (run id sg-update-2026-03-18-09-20)
aditya: rule added.
maria: re-running curl from pod -> `* Connected to 10.0.45.12 port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK >` :thumbsup:
kate: Nice. For the long term we should either: a) Have PrivateLink SGs include cluster pod CIDR via IaC when we onboard a cluster, or b) enforce SNAT so source is node IP (which our endpoint SG already allows). Which approach aligns with current infra policy?
chris: Our terraform modules for vpce currently only accept VPC CIDRs. We need to extend them to accept a list of extra trusted CIDRs (pod CIDR or peered CIDRs). I'll create a ticket.
aditya: Note: if we add many clusters with different pod CIDRs, SG rules will grow. Re-enabling SNAT on CNI might be simpler for scale, but may break some services that rely on client source IP. We should document tradeoffs.
maria: Created a short postmortem in #incidents with command history and the quick fix. I'll link the ticket to infra-vpce tf module.\oncall: ping @aditya for followup to decide SNAT vs SG update.
aditya: Will start a RFC PR on the terraform module and set up a runbook: "PrivateLink endpoints + pod IPs".
kate: Also add automatic alarms: if more than 5% of connections to a vpce fail with TLS handshake for >5min, create an alert.\maria: Thanks everyone, unblocked. Leaving the temporary SG rule and we can cleanup after RFC.
infra-bot: incident-created id=INC-2026-0318-07 by maria
chris: Created TF ticket INFRA-472: "vpce module: allow extra trusted CIDRs (pod/peering)" and linked PR to runbook.
aditya: Followup tasks: 1) RFC for SNAT vs SG (owner aditya), 2) TF change (owner chris), 3) Add alert (owner kate).
maria: closing thread, will update INCIDENT with final resolution once RFC decided. :white_check_mark:
